name: Canadian Power-Assisted Bicycle
description: Canada's federal e-bike definition, which the provinces built their e-bike laws on: a pedal bicycle on no more than three wheels with electric motors totalling 500 W or less that stop assisting at 32 km/h.

restrictions.rule: Steering handlebars, pedals, no more than three wheels, and capable of being propelled by muscular power
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: One or more electric motors with a total continuous power output rating, measured at the shaft, of 500 W or less
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Assistance engaged by pedalling stops as soon as pedalling stops; assistance engaged by a throttle stops as soon as the brakes are applied
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: The motor can't provide further assistance once the bicycle reaches 32 km/h on level ground
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Needed a motor on/off switch separate from the throttle, or a mechanism that keeps the motor from engaging below 3 km/h
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Needed a label permanently affixed by the manufacturer stating, in English and French, that it is a power-assisted bicycle
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Excluded from the federal motorcycle definition, so no Canada Motor Vehicle Safety Standard ever applied to it
restrictions.citation: Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations, C.R.C., c. 1038, s. 2(1), before SOR/2020-22

restrictions.rule: Repealed from the Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations on February 4, 2021: there's no longer a federal e-bike definition or label
Transport Canada no longer assesses e-bikes against it
Provincial laws such as Ontario's Highway Traffic Act still define their e-bikes by reference to it
restrictions.citation: Highway Traffic Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.8, s. 1(1)

restrictions.rule: At import, Transport Canada treats a pedal bicycle with motor assist unable to exceed 32 km/h as non-regulated, assesses one built like a scooter, motorcycle or motor tricycle as that class whatever its speed, and treats a faster one with off-road characteristics as a restricted-use vehicle
Where e-bikes may be ridden is left to provincial, territorial and local governments
In national parks, Parks Canada allows only pedal-assist e-bikes meeting this definition, on designated bike trails at select parks; e-bikes with a throttle may be ridden only on roads
